sections.markdown:
## C — Applying for your license: document checklist, citizenship and identity proof, residency, Social Security numbers, fees, new residents, military, renewal and address changes
Knowledge domain: what a Tennessee applicant must bring and prove before any license is issued — citizenship or legal presence, identity, name changes, residency and Social Security number — plus the fee schedule, new-resident and military rules, renewal, late fees and address-change duties.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Every document on the application checklist must be an original or a certified copy; faxes and photocopies are turned away. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Applicants bring two proofs of Tennessee residency showing their name and street address, with no post office boxes, and each must be current, meaning dated within the last 4 months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
An applicant under 18 also needs a Teenage Affidavit for financial responsibility, plus proof of relationship such as custody, adoption or marriage papers when the signing guardian or step-parent is not named on school attendance records. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
An applicant under 18 needs proof of school attendance or progress, such as Form SF1010 completed by the principal or guidance teacher, signed and dated within the past 30 days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
A teen moving past the learner permit must submit form SF-1256 certifying 50 hours of behind-the-wheel experience, after holding the permit for six months. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A02
A new resident's valid license from the former state can prove identity, but it never proves US citizenship or lawful permanent residency. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A02
Every supporting document for a name change must be an original or certified legal paper, and name changes are never accepted by mail. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A02
Proof of US citizenship or lawful permanent residency is required of first-time applicants, new and returning residents, anyone reinstating after a revocation, suspension or cancellation, and anyone licensed since January 1, 2001 who is renewing for the first time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A02
An applicant who has only temporary legal presence cannot get a regular license or ID, but may qualify for a Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License by proving authorized stay. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A02
A TDL or TID applicant must still meet every Tennessee examination requirement for driving Class XD or Class XM vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
Accepted proof of citizenship or permanent residency includes a certified birth certificate from a US state or territory, a valid US passport, a Certificate of Citizenship or Naturalization, and an I-551 Permanent Resident card. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A03
The examiner asks for two identity items, and an original applicant must supply at least one from the Primary list, with the second from either list. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A03
Applicants for a duplicate or renewal of an existing Tennessee license or ID may supply any 2 identity items from either list. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A03
New residents must hand in the license from their former state, and if it was lost they provide the same two identity items as an original applicant. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A03
A birth certificate must be certified, sealed and issued by an authorized agency such as the Bureau of Vital Statistics, and hospital-issued or baptismal certificates are refused. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A03
An expired passport is not accepted, and a passport, birth certificate or license not written in English must come with a Certificate of Accurate Translation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A04
Acceptable residency proofs include a current utility bill with its postmarked envelope, a bank statement, a signed lease or mortgage, an insurance policy, Tennessee vehicle or voter registration, a W-2, or a property tax receipt from within the last year. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A04
A utility initial deposit receipt, bank checks and insurance wallet cards do not count as proof of residency. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A04
Residency proof is demanded from first-time, new-resident and returning-resident applicants for every ID, TDL, permit and license class, even if they once held a Tennessee license before moving away. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A04
Residency documents may name the applicant, the applicant's spouse, or for a minor a parent or legal guardian, and relationship is then shown with a certified marriage certificate or long-form birth certificate. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A04
Tennessee law requires your Social Security number on the application whenever the US Government has issued you one, and the number is kept on your record but never printed on the license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A04
If the Social Security number does not match federal records, the examiner asks for more proof and may send you to the Social Security Administration before accepting the application. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A05
Someone never issued a Social Security number must sign a sworn affidavit in person before an examiner or notary, under penalty of perjury, and must sign a new one with every later application. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A05
Since January 1, 2016, licenses for people over 21 run eight years from the issue date, so they usually no longer expire on a birthday. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A05
A Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License runs for the authorized stay up to five years at a fixed twenty-eight-dollar base rate regardless of duration, plus any applicable GDL, motorcycle, or multi-type fees [A05].
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A05
New or returning residents holding another state's license must get a Tennessee license within 30 days of establishing residency. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A05
Every new or returning resident takes a Tennessee vision screening at the Driver Service Center. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A05
A new or returning resident whose out-of-state license expired more than six months ago must pass the knowledge exam, the road skills test and the vision screening. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A05
New residents arriving from other countries take the vision screening, knowledge exam and road skills test, and they may keep their foreign license. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A05
A Tennessee license held by a member of the US Armed Forces stays valid past its printed expiration while the person is on active duty based outside Tennessee and the license is not surrendered, canceled or suspended. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A06
On the standard eight-year fee table, a Class D operator license costs $28.00 with a minimum age of 16, and a learner permit for someone under 18 costs $10.50 for one year with a minimum age of 15. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A06
Active-duty personnel stationed outside Tennessee may have Code 30 added to the license to show it does not expire, by bringing their military orders and paying the fee. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A06
After discharge, separation or reassignment back to Tennessee, the service member must renew within 60 days, and Fort Campbell counts as a Tennessee assignment. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A06
A lost, stolen or destroyed license, permit or ID can be replaced at any Driver Service Center or sometimes online, but TDLs and TIDs cannot be replaced online. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A06
A Class D license issued before January 1, 2016 normally expires after 5 years on your birthdate, while permits normally expire one year after issuance. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A06
The Department mails a courtesy renewal notice eight to ten weeks before your license expires, though you can renew without it. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A07
A license expired more than 30 days carries a $5.00 late fee, which doubles to $10.00 after six months, and after five years you must also pass the vision, knowledge and skills tests. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A07
There is no grace period: once your license expires you may not drive, and you face the same penalties as someone never licensed. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A07
State law requires you to report a residence address change to the Department of Safety within 10 days, even when the change comes from the Postal Service or a 9-1-1 district renaming rather than a move. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A07
Your license must show a legal residential address with house or apartment number, street, city and zip code, and a post office box alone is refused. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A07
The Graduated Driver License program does not apply to anyone 18 or older, or to anyone under 18 who has graduated high school or earned a GED. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0027]

Misconceptions: an out-of-state license proves who you are but not that you are a citizen; telling the Post Office about a move does not update your Department of Safety record; an expired license has no grace period; photocopies are refused even when they look official.
Mnemonics: two and two — two identity items and two residency proofs; Primary first for originals; report a new address before ten days pass.
Glossary: Primary identification means a document such as a certified birth certificate or passport that can stand first; Secondary identification means supporting items such as work IDs or tax forms; TDL and TID mean the temporary license and ID tied to authorized stay; Code Thirty means the military non-expiring license code.
Dynamic facts: every fee, the payment methods, websites and mailing addresses can change; confirm them on the Department of Safety and Homeland Security website before showing them to learners.

corpus_stability.reason: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual says its content is current as of July 1, 2022 and its back cover carries one March 2025 print authorization; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year, but the content date is old, so freshness is held as debt rather than assumed.
